headline: The Problems, Services & Recovery Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a companion your backup plan, check and correct an official report before you sign it, politely refuse an improper request, call emergency services and explain your documents to an official, and write a clear claim or report in Spanish.

lessons.title: Walk a New Travel Buddy Through Your Backup-Card Plan
lessons.objective: Explain step by step why you split cards and cash between bags, and check that your companion can repeat the plan.

words.note: Usual word in Chile and Peru.
la carterista for a woman.
Introduces a result: separo todo, por eso nunca pierdo todo.

words.en: First I separate the cards, and then I split the cash.
words.es: Primero separo las tarjetas, y luego divido el efectivo.
words.note: Informal: you're talking to a friend.

words.en: I leave the backup one in the locker, because it's safer.
words.es: Dejo la de respaldo en el casillero, porque es más seguro.

words.en: That's why I never carry everything in the same place.
words.es: Por eso nunca llevo todo en el mismo lugar.

words.en: After that I write the bank's emergency number on paper.
words.es: Después anoto el número de emergencia del banco en papel.

words.en: If your wallet gets stolen, you still have another card.
words.es: Si te roban la billetera, todavía tienes otra tarjeta.

words.en: Can you explain the plan to me in your own words?
words.es: ¿Me puedes explicar el plan con tus palabras?
words.note: Informal tú.

words.en: Let's see, where would you keep the emergency cash?
words.es: A ver, ¿dónde guardarías el dinero de emergencia?

words.en: Exactly, that's how you do it!

lessons.speaking: You are the experienced traveler, and the AI is Ignacio, a travel buddy who keeps everything in one wallet: explain your backup-card plan step by step with primero, luego, porque and por eso, then ask him to repeat the plan back to you.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero guardo una tarjeta en la mochila, luego…, porque…, por eso…)

examples.es: Primero guardo una tarjeta en el bolsillo interior, y luego llevo la otra en la billetera.
examples.en: First I keep one card in the inside pocket, and then I carry the other one in my wallet.

examples.es: Un carterista solo puede llevarse una parte; por eso separo todo.
examples.en: A pickpocket can only take one part; that's why I split everything up.

lessons.title: Read the Phone Shop's eSIM Activation Sheet
lessons.objective: Read a printed eSIM activation sheet with the clerk and explain its general rules back in your own words.

words.note: In Colombia, shops often call the phone el equipo.

words.en: It says here the code is scanned only once, right?
words.es: Aquí dice que el código se escanea una sola vez, ¿verdad?

words.en: If the phone gets reset, what happens to the profile?
words.es: Si se restablece el equipo, ¿qué pasa con el perfil?

words.en: So, if the profile is deleted, it can't be recovered.
words.es: O sea, si se borra el perfil, no se recupera.

words.en: Let me check I understood: you need wifi to install it.
words.es: A ver si entendí: se necesita wifi para instalarla.

words.en: Is there an extra charge for a new code?
words.es: ¿Se cobra un costo adicional por un código nuevo?

words.en: Is my phone compatible with eSIM?
Could you explain it more slowly, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo puede explicar más despacio, por favor?
words.note: Formal usted, normal with a clerk in Colombia.

lessons.speaking: You are the customer, and the AI is Valentina, a phone-shop clerk in Bogotá: read the eSIM activation sheet with her, explain each rule back using impersonal se and si + present, and ask what happens to the profile if the phone gets reset.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se escanea el código una vez; si se borra el perfil, no se recupera)

examples.es: Se escanea el código QR una sola vez.
examples.en: The QR code is scanned only once.

examples.es: Si se borra el perfil, no se recupera con el mismo código.
examples.en: If the profile is deleted, it can't be recovered with the same code.

lessons.title: Show Your Friend How to Lock a Lost Phone Remotely
lessons.objective: Guide a friend through remotely locking and marking a lost phone, using clear commands with pronouns.

words.note: Chile says el computador; Mexico says la computadora.
cerrar sesión = to log out.
Usual word for password in Chile.

words.en: Open an incognito window and sign in to your account.
words.es: Abre una ventana de incógnito y entra a tu cuenta.
words.note: Informal tú with a friend.

words.en: Type it while covering the keyboard with your hand.
words.es: Escríbela tapando el teclado con la mano.

words.en: Don't give it to anyone, not even me.
words.es: No se la des a nadie, ni siquiera a mí.

words.en: Mark it as lost and add a contact number.
words.es: Márcalo como perdido y pon un número de contacto.

words.en: Don't erase it yet; that way we can see where it is.
words.es: No lo borres todavía; así vemos dónde está.

words.en: When we finish, log out; don't leave it open.
words.es: Cuando terminemos, cierra la sesión; no la dejes abierta.

words.en: Excuse me, could you give us a little privacy, please?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿nos da un poco de privacidad, por favor?
words.note: Formal usted, for the café owner.

lessons.speaking: You are the friend who knows the steps, and the AI is Paula, who lost her phone: guide her on a borrowed computer to lock it and mark it as lost with commands like bloquéalo, márcalo como perdido and no lo borres todavía, keeping her password private.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (bloquéalo, márcalo como perdido, no lo borres todavía, no se la des a nadie)

examples.es: Bloquéalo desde el navegador y márcalo como perdido.
examples.en: Lock it from the browser and mark it as lost.

examples.es: No se la muestres a nadie; escríbela en privado.
examples.en: Don't show it to anyone; type it in private.

lessons.title: Read Your Police Report Copy Before You Sign It
lessons.objective: Check every line of a printed police report and politely ask for corrections before you sign it.

words.note: In Spain, hurto is theft without force; robo involves force or violence.
la denunciante for a woman.
Formal police wording in Spain.
Spain says el móvil, not el celular.
Spain usage.

words.en: Before signing, may I read it carefully?
words.es: Antes de firmar, ¿me deja leerla con calma?
words.note: Formal usted with an officer.

words.en: Excuse me, there's a mistake in the date here.
words.es: Perdone, aquí hay un error en la fecha.
words.note: Perdone is the polite Spain form of excuse me.

words.en: It happened on March 14, not the 15th.
words.es: Los hechos fueron el 14 de marzo, no el 15.

words.en: I didn't have a camera in the backpack; it needs to be removed.
words.es: No llevaba ninguna cámara en la mochila; hay que quitarla.

words.en: We also need to check the list of items, please.
words.es: Hay que revisar también la relación de objetos, por favor.

words.en: Could you correct it before I sign?
After correcting it, will you print me a new copy?
words.es: Después de corregirlo, ¿me imprime una copia nueva?

words.en: Could you give me the report number, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar el número de atestado, por favor?

lessons.speaking: You are the theft victim, and the AI is Agente Herrero at a Madrid police station: read your printed report line by line, politely point out anything wrong and ask for corrections before you sign, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de firmar hay que revisar la fecha; después de corregirlo, firmo)

examples.es: Antes de firmar, hay que revisar la fecha de los hechos.
examples.en: Before signing, you have to check the date of the incident.

examples.es: Después de corregir la relación de objetos, firmo la denuncia.
examples.en: After correcting the list of items, I'll sign the report.

lessons.title: Wool Sweater Came Back Shrunk: Propose a Fair Fix
lessons.objective: Explain what you dropped off and what came back, then propose a reasonable solution to the laundry attendant.

words.note: Common word in Argentina for a laundry service.
Argentina says pulóver; Mexico says suéter.
Argentina says el talle; most other countries say la talla.
Use la dueña if the owner is a woman.

words.en: When I dropped it off on Monday, it was perfect.
words.es: Cuando lo dejé el lunes, estaba perfecto.

words.en: The ticket says cold wash, but it came out shrunk.
words.es: El ticket dice lavado en frío, pero salió encogido.

words.en: It used to fit me well; now the sleeves reach my elbow.
words.es: Antes me quedaba bien; ahora las mangas me llegan al codo.

words.en: I'm not blaming you; I just want a fair solution.
words.es: No la culpo a usted; solo quiero una solución justa.
words.note: Formal. Use la for a woman addressed as usted, lo for a man.

words.en: Could you refund the wash, at least?
words.es: ¿Podrían reembolsar el lavado, por lo menos?
words.note: Formal. Conditional softens the request.

words.en: A discount on the next wash would seem fair to me.
words.es: Me parecería justo un descuento en el próximo lavado.

words.en: Would it be possible to talk to the owner tomorrow?
words.es: ¿Sería posible hablar con el dueño mañana?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Could you write down the complaint with your name and the date?
words.es: ¿Me podría anotar el reclamo con su nombre y la fecha?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the customer, and the AI is Marcela, the laundry attendant: explain what you dropped off and how it came back using the preterite and imperfect (cuando lo dejé, estaba…), then propose a fair fix with the conditional (¿podrían…?, me parecería justo…).

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (cuando lo dejé, estaba perfecto; ¿podrían reembolsar el lavado?)

examples.es: Mientras usted buscaba el ticket, vi que la etiqueta decía lavado a mano.
examples.en: While you were looking for the ticket, I saw that the label said hand wash.

examples.es: ¿Podrían devolverme el costo del lavado?
examples.en: Could you give me back the cost of the wash?

lessons.title: Passport Photos Rejected: Compare Faster Options
lessons.objective: Find out why your photos were rejected and compare the nearby options before the window closes.

words.note: Mexico says lentes; Spain says gafas.

words.en: Can you tell me exactly why they were rejected?
words.es: ¿Me puede decir exactamente por qué las rechazaron?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: According to the consulate's list, what size do they require?
words.es: Según la lista del consulado, ¿qué tamaño piden?

words.en: What time does the window close today?
words.es: ¿A qué hora cierran la ventanilla hoy?

words.en: The booth is going to be faster than the studio.
words.es: La cabina va a ser más rápida que el estudio.

words.en: But the studio will be safer, because they know the requirements.
words.es: Pero el estudio será más seguro, porque conocen los requisitos.

words.en: Is there a studio nearby that knows these requirements?
words.es: ¿Hay algún estudio cerca que conozca estos requisitos?

words.en: I'm going to take off my glasses for the new photo.
words.es: Voy a quitarme los lentes para la foto nueva.

words.en: If I come back before closing, will you be the one helping me?
words.es: Si regreso antes del cierre, ¿me va a atender usted?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Lucía, the consulate clerk: ask exactly why your photos were rejected, then compare the booth and the studio with ir a + infinitive, the future and comparisons (más rápido que, más seguro que) before closing time.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (el estudio va a tardar más que la cabina, pero será más seguro que cumpla)

examples.es: El estudio va a tardar más que la cabina, pero será más seguro.
examples.en: The studio is going to take longer than the booth, but it will be safer.

examples.es: Regresaré antes del cierre con fotos que cumplan con la lista.
examples.en: I'll come back before closing with photos that meet the list.

lessons.title: Help a Robbed Stranger Talk to Bus Station Security
lessons.objective: Help a robbed tourist tell security what happened, with exact times, bus numbers and contact numbers.

words.note: Argentina says ómnibus or micro for long-distance buses.
Argentine term for the numbered bay where buses load.
Argentina. In Buenos Aires a city bus is el colectivo.
Use la guardia for a woman.
Argentina says boletería; Mexico says taquilla.
Argentina says campera; Mexico says chamarra.

words.en: Excuse me, he doesn't speak Spanish; I'll translate for him.
words.es: Disculpe, él no habla español; yo le traduzco.
words.note: Formal.
Say times clearly: las diecisiete cuarenta.

words.en: He put the bag on the floor and someone took it.
words.es: Puso el bolso en el piso y alguien se lo llevó.

words.en: First he said platform 12, but now he says 14.
words.es: Primero dijo la dársena 12, pero ahora dice la 14.

words.en: One moment, I'll check it against his ticket.
words.es: Un momento, lo confirmo con su boleto.
El teléfono de su hotel es el 261 555 0147.
words.note: Read numbers in pairs or small groups and repeat them back.

words.en: Can you check the cameras at that platform, please?
words.es: ¿Pueden revisar las cámaras de esa dársena, por favor?

words.en: What do we need to do now for the police report?
words.es: ¿Qué tenemos que hacer ahora para la denuncia?

lessons.speaking: You are helping Hans, a robbed tourist, and the AI is Ramiro, the terminal security guard: tell what happened in the preterite (bajó, puso, se lo llevó) and give the bus number, times and contact number clearly, repeating digits back.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (bajó del bus 214 a las 17:40, el teléfono de contacto es…)

examples.es: Llegó a la terminal a las 17:30 y compró el boleto en la boletería.
examples.en: He arrived at the terminal at 17:30 and bought the ticket at the ticket office.

examples.es: Un hombre con gorra roja agarró el bolso y salió hacia la dársena 9.
examples.en: A man in a red cap grabbed the bag and headed toward platform 9.

lessons.title: Say No When the Hostel Wants to Keep Your Passport
lessons.objective: Politely refuse to leave your passport as a deposit, advise your roommate, and offer an acceptable alternative.

words.note: Spain's usual word for a security deposit.
Spain says importe; Latin America says monto.
Say it de-ene-i.
Spain. Businesses must provide it if a customer asks.
Use el compañero de habitación for a man.
Use la recepcionista for a woman.

words.en: I'm sorry, but I can't leave you my original passport.
words.es: Lo siento, pero no puedo dejarle mi pasaporte original.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Clara, don't give it to him yet; wait a moment.
words.es: Clara, no se lo des todavía; espera un momento.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Clara, I don't recommend that you leave it with him.
words.es: Clara, no te recomiendo que se lo dejes.
words.note: Informal. Subjunctive after no recomiendo que.

words.en: If they lose it, we can't travel or go home.
words.es: Si lo pierden, no podemos viajar ni volver a casa.

words.en: I can leave you a cash deposit; is that OK with you?
words.es: Puedo dejarle una fianza en efectivo, ¿le parece?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would a scanned copy and a card pre-authorization work for you?
words.es: ¿Le sirve una copia escaneada y una preautorización en la tarjeta?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Can you confirm it in writing, with the amount?
words.es: ¿Me lo puede confirmar por escrito, con el importe?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Tomás, the hostel receptionist: politely refuse to leave your original passport, advise your roommate Clara with negative commands (no se lo des) and no te recomiendo que + subjunctive, and offer an alternative such as a cash deposit.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo dejes; no recomiendo que se quede con el original)

examples.es: No lo dejes en recepción, Clara; guárdalo en la caja fuerte.
examples.en: Don't leave it at reception, Clara; keep it in the safe.

examples.es: No recomiendo que te quedes sin pasaporte esta noche.
examples.en: I don't recommend that you go without your passport tonight.

lessons.title: Feedback for a Friend Who Left the Bag Unattended
lessons.objective: Give a friend kind, honest feedback about leaving a daypack unattended, and recommend changes without blame.

words.note: Common in Spain for a harmless lapse; softer than descuido.
Spain, informal: echar la bronca = to tell someone off.
In Spain, the outdoor seating area of a café or bar.
Spain word; in Latin America people say el cierre.
Spain: robo por tirón = a snatch theft.

words.en: Diego, I'm not telling you off; I just want us to talk.
words.es: Diego, no es una bronca; solo quiero que hablemos.
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: I know it was only a minute, but a minute is enough.
words.es: Ya sé que fue solo un minuto, pero basta con un minuto.

words.en: I don't blame you; it's happened to me too.
words.es: No te culpo; a mí también me ha pasado.

words.en: I recommend you always keep it in sight.
words.es: Te recomiendo que la tengas siempre a la vista.

words.en: Please zip it up before you sit down.
words.es: Te pido que cierres la cremallera antes de sentarte.

words.en: I'd rather we take turns carrying it, okay?
words.es: Prefiero que la llevemos por turnos, ¿vale?
words.note: ¿Vale? is the everyday Spain tag for okay.

words.en: How about we talk it over calmly?
words.es: ¿Qué te parece si lo hablamos con calma?

lessons.speaking: You are Diego's friend, and the AI is Diego, who left the shared daypack on a café chair yesterday: give him kind, honest feedback and suggest new habits with quiero que + subjunctive and te recomiendo que la lleves delante, without blaming him.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que estés tranquilo; te recomiendo que la lleves delante)

examples.es: Quiero que estés tranquilo; no te estoy echando la bronca.
examples.en: I want you to be calm; I'm not telling you off.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que la lleves delante cuando haya mucha gente.
examples.en: I recommend you carry it in front when it's crowded.

lessons.title: Two Roommates, One Missing Charger: Settle It
lessons.objective: Listen to both roommates, report each version to the manager, and help everyone agree on a fair next step.

words.note: For a woman: la compañera de cuarto.
Uruguay and Argentina; Spain says la litera.
Rioplatense usage; elsewhere it only means sneaker.
Common in Uruguay and Argentina, said with a Spanish accent.
Agrees with the person: Joaquín estaba dormido, Camila estaba dormida.

words.en: Ernesto, excuse me, there's a problem in room 6.
words.es: Ernesto, disculpe, hay un problema en el cuarto 6.
words.note: Formal, to the manager.

words.en: Camila said the charger was plugged in next to her bunk.
words.es: Camila dijo que el cargador estaba enchufado junto a su cucheta.

words.en: Joaquín said he was asleep and didn't see anything.
words.es: Joaquín dijo que estaba dormido y que no vio nada.

words.en: She said she had used it at 22:00.
words.es: Ella dijo que lo había usado a las 22:00.

words.en: He said his charger was a different model.
words.es: Él contó que su cargador era de otro modelo.

words.en: Maybe it's a misunderstanding; nobody is accusing anybody.
words.es: Capaz que es un malentendido; nadie está acusando a nadie.
words.note: Capaz que = maybe, very common in Uruguay.

words.en: Could you check the lost and found, please?
words.es: ¿Podría revisar los objetos perdidos, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: How about we all look in the common room together?
words.es: ¿Les parece si buscamos juntos en la sala común?
words.note: To both roommates (ustedes).

lessons.speaking: You are a guest in the dorm, and the AI is night manager Ernesto: calmly tell him what Camila and Joaquín each said, using reported speech like dijo que estaba and dijo que dormía, and propose a fair next step everyone can agree on.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Camila dijo que el cargador estaba en su cama; Joaquín dijo que dormía)

examples.es: Camila dijo que el cargador estaba en su cucheta a las 23:00.
examples.en: Camila said the charger was on her bunk at 23:00.

examples.es: Joaquín dijo que dormía y que no tocó nada.
examples.en: Joaquín said he was sleeping and didn't touch anything.

lessons.title: Keep Your Group Going After the Wallet Theft
lessons.objective: Encourage your travel group after a theft and commit to a clear plan for the rest of the day.

words.note: ¡Ánimo! alone means Cheer up! or Hang in there!
Informal.
In Mexico, coraje usually means anger: me da coraje = it makes me mad.
Mexico: tengo muchos pendientes = I have a lot to do.

words.en: the prosecutor's office (where you file a report)

words.note: Mexico's word for a city's central plaza.
In Mexico, la comida is the main afternoon meal.
Use juntas if the whole group is women.

words.en: Andrés, you're not alone; we're here with you.
words.es: Andrés, no estás solo; aquí estamos contigo.
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: This afternoon we'll go to the prosecutor's office to file the report.
words.es: Hoy por la tarde iremos a la Fiscalía a levantar la denuncia.
words.note: Levantar una denuncia = to file a report, standard in Mexico.

words.en: Right now we'll call the bank to block your card.
words.es: Ahora mismo llamaremos al banco para bloquear tu tarjeta.

words.en: I'll lend you money until the transfer arrives.
words.es: Yo te prestaré dinero hasta que llegue la transferencia.

words.en: Sofía, will you take care of making the to-do list?
words.es: Sofía, ¿tú te encargas de hacer la lista de pendientes?
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Hang in there, we've already done the hardest part.
words.es: Ánimo, ya hicimos lo más difícil.

words.en: Let's not cancel yet; we'll decide calmly tomorrow.
words.es: No cancelemos todavía; decidiremos mañana con calma.

words.en: What worries you most right now?
words.es: ¿Qué es lo que más te preocupa ahorita?
words.note: Ahorita = right now, very Mexican.

lessons.speaking: You are Andrés and Sofía's travel friend, and the AI is Andrés, whose wallet was just stolen in the zócalo: encourage him with ánimo and vas muy bien, and set out a clear plan for the rest of the day with future commitments like iremos a la Fiscalía and lo resolveremos juntos.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana iremos al banco; lo resolveremos juntos; ánimo, vas muy bien)

examples.es: Mañana iremos al banco y pediremos una tarjeta nueva.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll go to the bank and ask for a new card.

examples.es: Ánimo, Andrés; lo resolveremos juntos.
examples.en: Hang in there, Andrés; we'll sort it out together.

lessons.title: Bag Left in a Taxi: Friend, Dispatcher, Driver
lessons.objective: Switch between tú and usted as you talk to a friend, a taxi dispatcher and the driver to get a bag back.

words.note: In Chile people often just say la central.
Chile word; Mexico says la placa.
Chile also says la maleta for the car trunk.
Va apurado = he's in a hurry; for a woman, apurada.

words.en: Hey, Elena, breathe; we're going to find it.
words.es: Oye, Elena, respira; lo vamos a encontrar.
words.note: Informal (tú), to a friend.

words.en: Good afternoon, Mrs. Pizarro, I'd like to know if a bag was found.
words.es: Buenas tardes, señora Pizarro, quisiera saber si encontraron un bolso.
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: We took the dispatch taxi at 15:20 in Providencia.
words.es: Tomamos el radiotaxi a las 15:20 en Providencia.

words.en: Would you mind giving me the car's license plate?
words.es: ¿Le importaría darme la patente del auto?
words.note: Formal softener.

words.en: Don Ramón, sorry for the trouble; I know you're in a hurry.
words.es: Don Ramón, disculpe la molestia; sé que va apurado.
words.note: Formal; Don + first name shows respect.

words.en: It's black and has a red keychain.
words.es: Es negro y tiene un llavero rojo.

words.en: Thank you so much, really; will you accept a tip?
words.es: Muchas gracias, de verdad; ¿me acepta una propina?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Elena, can you check if anything is missing inside?
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are traveling with Elena, and the AI plays Elena, dispatcher Señora Pizarro and driver Don Ramón in turn: calm your friend with tú, then use usted and softeners like quisiera saber si… and ¿le importaría…? to get the bag back.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera saber si…; ¿le importaría…?; oye, tranquila, ya llamé)

examples.es: Señora Pizarro, quisiera saber si el conductor encontró un bolso negro.
examples.en: Mrs. Pizarro, I'd like to know if the driver found a black bag.

examples.es: Oye, tranquila, ya llamé a la central.
examples.en: Hey, relax, I already called the dispatch office.

lessons.title: Friend Fell on the Metro Stairs: Clinic Intake
lessons.objective: Tell the clinic step by step when and how your friend fell, and confirm what record you will get for insurance.

words.note: Also la baranda.
For a woman: la acompañante.
The usual Colombian term for a patient's clinic record.

words.en: At around 9, Owen slipped going down the stairs.
words.es: A eso de las 9, Owen se resbaló bajando las escaleras.
words.note: Formal: speaking to the receptionist.

words.en: Right after getting off the train, he stepped wrong on a step.
words.es: Justo después de bajar del tren, pisó mal un escalón.

words.en: He fell sideways and hit his wrist.
words.es: Se cayó de lado y se golpeó la muñeca.

words.en: A few minutes later, his ankle started to swell.
words.es: Unos minutos más tarde, el tobillo se le empezó a hinchar.

words.en: Since then he can't put weight on his foot.
words.es: Desde entonces no puede apoyar el pie.

words.en: He didn't lose consciousness, but he was dizzy for a while.
words.es: No perdió el conocimiento, pero estuvo mareado un rato.

words.en: Owen, the message you sent says 9:12, not 9:30.
words.es: Owen, el mensaje que mandaste dice 9:12, no 9:30.
words.note: Informal: tú with your friend.

words.en: Can you give me the medical record and the bill for the insurance?
words.es: ¿Me pueden dar la historia clínica y la factura para el seguro?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are Owen's travel companion, and the AI is Natalia, the receptionist at a Medellín urgent-care clinic: tell her step by step when and how Owen fell, using a eso de las…, justo después de…, unos minutos más tarde and desde entonces, then ask what record you'll get for insurance.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a eso de las nueve, justo después de bajar, unos minutos más tarde, desde entonces)

examples.es: A eso de las 9 bajamos del tren, y justo después se cayó.
examples.en: At around 9 we got off the train, and right after that he fell.

examples.es: Unos minutos más tarde ya no podía caminar, y desde entonces le duele.
examples.en: A few minutes later he couldn't walk anymore, and it has hurt since then.

lessons.title: Nearly Took a Fake Taxi: Debrief with the Hostel
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss with a fake airport taxi without blame, and agree on what to tell other guests.

words.note: Peru: someone who pulls customers toward a business or car.
Latin America stresses chofer on the last syllable.
Peru: a work ID card with a photo.

words.en: I almost got into an unlicensed taxi in the arrivals area.
words.es: Casi subo a un taxi informal en la zona de llegadas.

words.en: I very nearly handed the driver my suitcase.
words.es: Por poco le doy la maleta al chofer.

words.en: If I had gotten in, I could have ended up far away without my suitcase.
words.es: Si hubiera subido, podría haber terminado lejos y sin maleta.

words.en: I asked for his ID badge and he didn't know what to say.
words.es: Le pedí el fotocheck y no supo qué decir.

words.en: Lucas, relax, it wasn't your fault; it happened to both of us.
words.es: Lucas, tranquilo, no fue tu culpa; nos pasó a los dos.
words.note: Informal: tú with your friend.

words.en: We're not looking for someone to blame; we just don't want it to happen to anyone.
words.es: No buscamos culpables; solo queremos que no le pase a nadie.

words.en: Rosa, what do you think about putting a sign at the front desk?
words.es: Rosa, ¿le parece si ponemos un letrero en la recepción?
words.note: Formal: usted with the manager.

words.en: Let's tell the group to use only the taxi counter.
words.es: Avisemos en el grupo que solo usen el módulo de taxis.

lessons.speaking: You are a hostel guest, and the AI is Rosa, the hostel manager in Lima: talk through how you nearly took an unlicensed airport taxi without blaming anyone, using casi, por poco and si hubiera…, podría haber…, and agree on what to tell other guests.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (casi subo; por poco le doy la maleta; si hubiera subido, podría haber…)

examples.es: Casi subo al carro, pero Lucas vio que no tenía fotocheck.
examples.en: I almost got in the car, but Lucas saw he had no ID badge.

examples.es: Si hubiéramos subido, podría haber pasado algo grave.
examples.en: If we had gotten in, something serious could have happened.

lessons.title: Call 112 for a Stranger Who Collapsed in the Plaza
lessons.objective: Call emergency services, give the location clearly and follow the operator's instructions until help arrives.

words.note: In Spain often called el DEA.
Spain: the sign on the wall with the street name.
Spain: the street door of a building; give its number.

words.en: There's an older man unconscious on the ground in a plaza.
words.es: Hay un señor mayor inconsciente en el suelo de una plaza.
words.note: Formal: usted with the operator.

words.en: One moment, I'm going to look at the street sign.
words.es: Un momento, voy a mirar la placa de la calle.

words.en: We're next to the fountain, across from the tram stop.
words.es: Estamos junto a la fuente, frente a la parada del tranvía.

words.en: Yes, he's breathing, but he doesn't respond when I talk to him.
words.es: Sí, respira, pero no responde cuando le hablo.

words.en: If he stops breathing, I'll tell you right away.
words.es: Si deja de respirar, se lo diré enseguida.

words.en: Okay, I'll put him on his side and stay with him.
words.es: Vale, lo pongo de lado y me quedo con él.
words.note: Vale is the usual Spain 'okay'.

words.en: Can you repeat that more slowly, please?
words.es: ¿Puede repetir eso más despacio, por favor?

words.en: I can hear the siren now; I'll wave them over.
words.es: Ya oigo la sirena; voy a hacerles señas.

lessons.speaking: You are a passer-by in a Zaragoza plaza, and the AI is the 112 operator: report that an older man has collapsed, give the exact location, and follow instructions, using si + present → future (si no responde, se lo diré) and short replies to commands like quédese con él.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short phone commands (si no responde, se lo diré; quédese con él; dígame la calle)

examples.es: Si encuentro la placa, le diré la calle exacta.
examples.en: If I find the sign, I'll tell you the exact street.

examples.es: Quédese con él y dígame si respira.
examples.en: Stay with him and tell me if he's breathing.

lessons.title: Missing Entry Stamp: Explain It at Migration
lessons.objective: Formally explain to a migration officer how your emergency passport was issued and show the supporting papers.

words.note: For a woman: la oficial de migración.
Colombia says expedición for when a document is issued.
Colombian usage for the papers that back up a request.
Colombian term; elsewhere la tarjeta de embarque.

words.en: Let me explain, sir: the stamp is in the stolen passport.
words.es: Le explico, señor: el sello está en el pasaporte robado.
words.note: Formal: usted with the officer.

words.en: The police report was filed on May 3 in Bogotá.
words.es: La denuncia se presentó el 3 de mayo en Bogotá.

words.en: The document was issued at the embassy 2 days later.
words.es: El documento se emitió en la embajada 2 días después.

words.en: Attached here are the police report and the embassy certificate.
words.es: Aquí se adjuntan la denuncia y la constancia de la embajada.
words.note: Plural verb (se adjuntan) because two documents follow.

words.en: The copy of my original passport is on my phone.
words.es: La copia del pasaporte original está en mi celular.

words.en: My battery is low; would there be an outlet where I can charge it?
words.es: Tengo poca batería; ¿habría un tomacorriente donde pueda cargarlo?

words.en: Could you check my entry in the immigration record, please?
words.es: ¿Podría consultar mi ingreso en el registro migratorio, por favor?

words.en: Could you tell me if any other supporting document is needed?
words.es: ¿Me podría indicar si se necesita algún otro soporte?

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler, and the AI is officer Moreno at Cartagena airport migration: formally explain how your emergency passport was issued, using passive se (se presentó la denuncia, se emitió el documento, se adjunta la copia), and present your supporting papers.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se presentó la denuncia; se emitió el documento; se adjunta la copia)

examples.es: Se emitió el pasaporte de emergencia el 5 de mayo, según la constancia.
examples.en: The emergency passport was issued on May 5, according to the certificate.

examples.es: Se registró mi entrada en el pasaporte que me robaron.
examples.en: My entry was recorded in the passport that was stolen from me.

lessons.title: Write the Insurance Claim Summary for a Stolen Laptop
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal claim summary with the facts, the report number and the list of attachments.

words.note: For a man, say el ajustador de seguros.
In Mexico people also say la laptop.
In Mexico the Fiscalía opens this file and gives it a number when you report a crime.
Standard formal sign-off, written right before your name.

words.en: Dear Ms. Núñez, I am sending you a summary of what happened.
words.es: Estimada licenciada Núñez, le envío el resumen de lo ocurrido.
words.note: Formal. In Mexican business email, licenciada is a common polite title.

words.en: First, the computer was stolen on June 2.
words.es: En primer lugar, la computadora fue sustraída el 2 de junio.

words.en: Afterwards, I filed the report with the Jalisco Prosecutor's Office.
words.es: Posteriormente, presenté la denuncia ante la Fiscalía de Jalisco.

words.en: It should be noted that I do not have the original invoice.
words.es: Cabe señalar que no cuento con la factura original.

words.en: Therefore, I am attaching the bank statement as proof of payment.
words.es: Por lo tanto, adjunto el estado de cuenta como comprobante de pago.

words.en: Only the last 4 digits are visible on the bank statement.
words.es: En el estado de cuenta solo se ven los últimos 4 dígitos.
words.note: Cover the full card number before you send any document.

words.en: I am attaching the copy of the police report with the case file number.
words.es: Adjunto la copia de la denuncia con el número de carpeta.

words.en: Could you confirm whether the bank statement is enough?
words.es: ¿Podría confirmarme si el estado de cuenta es suficiente?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is insurance adjuster Patricia Núñez: read her your claim summary for the stolen laptop, ordering the facts with en primer lugar, posteriormente and por lo tanto, giving the report number and listing each attachment with adjunto.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, posteriormente, cabe señalar que, por lo tanto, adjunto)

examples.es: En primer lugar, el robo ocurrió el 2 de junio en el espacio de coworking.
examples.en: First, the theft occurred on June 2 in the coworking space.

examples.es: Por lo tanto, adjunto el estado de cuenta con los datos bancarios tapados.
examples.en: Therefore, I am attaching the bank statement with the bank details covered.

lessons.title: Text and Call the Host When Your Arrival Changes
lessons.objective: Send a clear message and leave a polite voice message to change your arrival date and ask about the host's options.

words.note: For a man, say el anfitrión.
Spain: piso means apartment.
Spain says billete; Latin America says boleto.

words.en: Hi, Beatriz, I'm writing to let you know about a change.
words.es: Hola, Beatriz, le escribo para avisarle de un cambio.
words.note: Formal (usted). Polite way to open a text to a host.

words.en: I pick up my passport on Thursday, so I'll arrive on Friday.
words.es: Recojo el pasaporte el jueves, así que llegaré el viernes.

words.en: Would it be possible to change the arrival to Friday the 12th?
words.es: ¿Sería posible cambiar la llegada al viernes 12?

words.en: I'm calling about the booking for the 11th; I'm running a day late.
words.es: Le llamo por la reserva del día 11; me retraso un día.
words.note: In Spain, le llamo is the usual polite form for calling someone.

words.en: Could you clarify whether the change has any cost?
words.es: ¿Me podría aclarar si el cambio tiene algún coste?
words.note: Spain says coste; Latin America says costo.

words.en: Sorry, I didn't quite understand whether you'd charge me for the first night.
words.es: Perdone, no me quedó claro si me cobraría la primera noche.

words.en: If it weren't possible, what options would I have?
words.es: Si no fuera posible, ¿qué opciones tendría?

words.en: I look forward to your reply; thank you very much.
words.es: Quedo atento a su respuesta; muchas gracias.
words.note: A woman writes quedo atenta.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is your host Beatriz in Cádiz: text her and then leave a voice message to move your arrival back a day, using le escribo para avisarle, ¿sería posible…? and quedo atento a su respuesta, and ask what options she can offer.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (le escribo para avisarle…; ¿sería posible…?; quedo atento a su respuesta)

examples.es: Le escribo para avisarle de que llegaré el viernes en lugar del jueves.
examples.en: I'm writing to let you know I'll arrive on Friday instead of Thursday.

examples.es: ¿Sería posible dejar las llaves en la caja de llaves?
examples.en: Would it be possible to leave the keys in the lockbox?

lessons.title: Collect Your Recovered Backpack at Lost Property
lessons.objective: Go over the release conditions with the clerk, check the contents together and close the case.

words.note: Spain: the stamped slip you keep as proof of a procedure.
Acta is feminine but takes el: el acta, las actas.
Spain: anotar una incidencia means to log a problem officially.
A public employee; for a woman, la funcionaria.
Firmar de conformidad = sign to confirm you agree.
Agrees with the noun: la mochila está intacta.

words.en: Would you give it to me provided I show the slip and my passport?
words.es: ¿Me la entregarían siempre que presente el resguardo y el pasaporte?
words.note: Siempre que + subjunctive = provided that.

words.en: I can describe the patch on the side pocket before we open it.
words.es: Puedo describirle el parche del bolsillo lateral antes de abrirla.

words.en: Could we check the contents together, one by one?
words.es: ¿Podríamos revisar el contenido juntos, uno por uno?

words.en: Excuse me, the external hard drive isn't on the inventory.
words.es: Perdone, en el inventario no aparece el disco duro externo.

words.en: Could you log it as an issue before I sign?
words.es: ¿Podría anotarlo como incidencia antes de que firme?
words.note: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

words.en: I'd sign off as long as what's missing is on record.
words.es: Firmaría la conformidad siempre que conste lo que falta.

words.en: I could show you a photo of me with the backpack, if that helps.
words.es: Le enseñaría una foto mía con la mochila, si le sirve.

words.en: Would you give me a copy of the form with the case number?
words.es: ¿Me daría una copia del acta con el número de expediente?

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is clerk Jordi Puig at Barcelona's lost-property office: confirm the release conditions using siempre que and con tal de que with the subjunctive, check the backpack's contents with him, and close the case with conditional requests like firmaría and ¿me daría…?

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (se lo entregaríamos siempre que presente…; lo firmaría siempre que esté todo)

examples.es: Se la entregaríamos siempre que presente un documento acreditativo.
examples.en: We would release it to you provided you show a supporting ID document.

examples.es: Firmaría el acta con tal de que conste la incidencia del disco duro.
examples.en: I'd sign the form as long as the hard drive issue is on record.

lessons.title: Capstone: Phone and Wallet Stolen Before Your Flight
lessons.objective: Handle a full recovery day: report, block, replace, explain, keep a companion going and write the day's summary.

words.note: Ecuador: Unidad de Policía Comunitaria, the local police post. Said as letters: u-pe-ce.
Ecuadorian; the verb is arranchar (me arrancharon el celular).

words.en: Officer, they snatched our phone and wallet in La Mariscal.
words.es: Agente, nos arrancharon el celular y la billetera en La Mariscal.
words.note: Formal: address the officer as agente.

words.en: Could you give me the police report before you close?
words.es: ¿Me podría dar el parte policial antes de que cierren?

words.en: Ms. Mónica, I need you to block the card permanently.
words.es: Señorita Mónica, necesito que bloquee la tarjeta de forma definitiva.
words.note: Formal. Never say a full card number or PIN aloud.

words.en: My flight leaves at 6:00; would it be possible to see me today?
words.es: Mi vuelo sale a las 6:00; ¿sería posible atenderme hoy?
words.note: Formal, for the consular worker.

words.en: Gabriela, sit down and drink some water; I'll call the bank.
words.es: Gabriela, siéntate y toma agua; yo llamo al banco.
words.note: Informal tú commands for a travel companion.

words.en: Gabriela, don't worry; we'll sort it out step by step.
words.es: Gabriela, no te preocupes; lo resolveremos paso a paso.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Could you charge the early-morning taxi to the room, please?
words.es: ¿Podría cargar el taxi de madrugada a la habitación, por favor?
words.note: Formal, for the hotel receptionist.

words.en: In summary, today the cards were blocked and the document was issued.
words.es: En resumen, hoy se bloquearon las tarjetas y se emitió el documento.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Agente Salazar, bank agent Mónica, consular worker Felipe and a hotel receptionist: narrate the theft, block the card, ask for travel papers with ¿sería posible…?, keep Gabriela going with tú commands, then summarize the day formally.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar (narration, subjunctive, conditional, formal register, commands)

examples.es: Cuando salimos del café, un hombre nos arranchó la billetera.
examples.en: When we left the café, a man snatched our wallet.

examples.es: Le agradecería que nos atendiera hoy, ya que el vuelo sale de madrugada.
examples.en: I'd appreciate it if you could see us today, since the flight leaves early in the morning.
